guards: Fabrication where it is hardest to notice - beside evidence that is real. The out-of-corpus case catches an invented citation when nothing was retrieved; this one catches it when two chunks were, which is the production shape: a model handed genuine snippets extends them with a dose threshold and a chunk id in the same house style. The critic has to resolve each guideline citation against the chunk ids actually retrieved rather than against the token pattern; a resolver that accepts any well-formed token ships the invented dosing line under a citation indistinguishable from the real one. It claims no more than that: the invented id is in neither the corpus nor the retrieved set, and a two-chunk corpus is smaller than topK, so here the corpus and the retrieved set are the same set and this case cannot tell a resolver reading the whole corpus from a correct one. That clause belongs to the three evidence-topk-* cases, whose drafts cite a real corpus chunk the topK cut left out.

evidence.intent: Two anticoagulation chunks retrieved and cited correctly on the first line; the second asserts a DOAC dose reduction citing a chunk id in neither the retrieved set nor the corpus. Asserts the real citation survives, the invented one is both absent from what shipped and present in the suppressed-claims list, and the dosing claim never reaches the clinician.
evidence.question: Testpatient Whiskey is on apixaban with a falling creatinine clearance - what do the guidelines say?

corpus.text: Direct oral anticoagulants require dose reduction or avoidance in renal impairment. Assess creatinine clearance before starting a DOAC and periodically thereafter.
For most patients with atrial fibrillation on warfarin, the target INR is 2.0 to 3.0.

model_script.text:
